mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month when trigger occurs (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 1.5% in the current month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 6.5% in the current month
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or at least not statistically different from zero during the subsequent window (p > 0.10), or UNRATE does not exceed 6.5% in the current month.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST index exceeds 1100 for two consecutive months, it signals a surge in industrial demand that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1100 for two consecutive months ending in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return occurs within 30 days after the second consecutive month of HOUST > 1100 (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 101.5 indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 101.5 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or at least not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during the same month INDPRO crosses below 101.5.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 233 suggests central bank disinflation efforts, which, if persistent, drive a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via rate-cut expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months ending in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the three-month CPIAUCSL decline window (mean p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward splits).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds 137,000 for a month, it reflects strong labor market absorption that precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates wage growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not positive or not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during the month PAYEMS crosses above 137,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above their respective 1% and 7% monthly moving averages for the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to conflicting signals of rate hikes and labor market cooling.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 1% AND UNRATE > 7% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from zero during the same month both proxies cross their thresholds (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by GDPC1 > 16,000 and HOUST > 900 for two consecutive months), a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as market confidence rebounds.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 16,000 AND HOUST > 900 for two consecutive months ending in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative throughout the two-month recovery window (mean p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward tests).
